annotations.title: Holdeth the ſeuen.
annotations.text: Much to be obſerued, that Chriſt hath ſuch care ouer the Church and the Biſhops thereof, <mn>◦</mn> that he is ſaid here to beare them vp in his right hand, and to walke in the middes of them: no doubt to vphold and preſerue them and to guide them in al truth.

annotations.title: Thy workes, labour, patience &c.
annotations.text: Things required in a Biſhop. firſt, good vvorkes, and great patience in tribulation. next, <mn>◦</mn> zeale and ſharpe diſcipline tovvard offenders is here comended in them. thirdly, wiſedom & diligence in trial of falſe Apoſtles and preachers comming in ſheepe-ſkinnes: vvhere is ſignified the watchful prouidence that ought to be in them, that Heretikes enter not into their flockes.

notes.text: Special vertues required in a Bishop.

annotations.title: Wil moue.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Note that the cauſe why God taketh the truth from certaine countries, and remoueth their Biſhops or Churches into captiuitie or deſolation, is the ſinne of the Prelates and people. And that is the cauſe (no doubt) that Chriſt hath taken avvay our golden candleſticke, that is, our Church in England. God graunt vs to remember our fall, to doe penance and the former workes of charitie vvhich our firſt Biſhops and Church were notable and renowmed for.

notes.text: Sinne is the cause that God taketh the Cath. faith from cuntries.

annotations.title: Becauſe thou hateſt.
annotations.text: Vve ſee here that of al things, Chriſtian people (ſpecially Biſhops) ſhould haue great zeale againſt Heretikes and hate them, <mn>◦</mn> that is, their vvicked doctrine and conditions, euen as God hateth them. for which onely zeale, our Lord ſaith here that he beareth vvith ſome Churches and Prelates, and ſaueth them from periſhing.

annotations.title: Of the Nicolaites.
annotations.text: Heretikes haue their callings of certaine perſons, as is noted at large Act. 11, 26. Theſe had their name of Nicolas, ◦ one of the 7 firſt Deacons that were choſen Act. 6. Who is thought to haue taught communitie of vvomen or vviues, and that it vvas lavvful to eate of meates offered to idols. Which later point is ſuch a thing, as if one ſhould hold it lawful to receiue the bread or vvine of the new Communion, vvhich is a kinde of Idolothyta, that is, idolatrous meates. for though ſuch creatures be good by creation, yet they be made execrable by profane bleſſings of Heretikes or Idolaters. And concerning the name of Nicolaites giuen here by our Lord him ſelf to thoſe Heretikes, it is a very paterne and marke vnto the faithful for euer, vvhat kinde of men they ſhould be, that ſhould be called after the like ſort, Arians, Macedonians, Neſtorians, Lutherans, Zuinglians, &c. See S. Hierom cont. Luſifer. in fine.

notes.text: Nicolaites the first Heretikes so called, as a paterne of Arians, Lutherans, and the like peculiar callings.

annotations.title: To caſt a ſcandal.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> Ioſephus vvriteth that when Balaam could not curſe Gods people, nor otherwiſe anoy them, he taught Balac a way how to ouerthrow them: <mn>[2]</mn> to vvit, by preſenting vnto them their Heathen vvomen very beautiful, and delicate diſhes of meate offered to Bel-phegor: that ſo being tempted they might fall to heatheniſh maners and diſpleaſe God. <mn>[3]</mn> To which craftie counſel of Balaam the Apoſtle reſembleth Heretikes fraude, vvho by offering of libertie of meate, women, Church goodes, breache of vowes, and ſuch other licentious allurements, cauſe many moe to fall, then by their preaching.

notes.text: Balaam ouercomming Gods people by persuasion of lecherie and bellicheere, was a type of Heretikes.

annotations.title: The vvoman Iezabel.
annotations.text: He warneth Biſhops to be zelous and ſtout againſt falſe Prophets and Heretikes of vvhat ſort ſoeuer, <mn>[1]</mn> by alluding couertly to the example of holy Elias that in zeale killed 450 falſe prophets of Iezabel, <mn>[2]</mn> and ſpared not Achab nor Iezabel them ſelues, <mn>[3]</mn> but told them to their faces that they troubled Iſrael, that is, the faithful people of God. And whether there were any ſuch great woman then, a furtherer and promotour of the Nicolaites, vvhom the Prophete ſhould here meane, it is hard to ſay.

annotations.title: She wil not repent.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> See free vvil here moſt plainely, and that God is not the proper cauſe of obduration or impenitence, but man him ſelf onely. Our Lord giueth ſinners ſo long life, ſpecially to expect their amendment: but Iezabel (to vvhom the Apoſtle here alludeth) would neuer repent.

notes.text: Free wil. God is not author of euil.

annotations.title: They that commit aduoutrie with her.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> Such as communicate with Heretikes, ſhal be damned (alas) vvith them. for, not onely ſuch as were in their hartes, of Iezabels religion, or inwardly beleeued in Baal, but ſuch as externally for feare vvorſhipped him (vvhich the Scriptures call, bowing of their knees to Baal) <mn>[2]</mn> are culpable. as now many bow their knees to the Communion, that bow not their hartes.

notes.text: They that communicate with Heretikes, shal be damned with them

annotations.title: I wil giue him power.
annotations.text: Obſerue that not onely Angels haue power and regiment ouer Countries vnder God, but now for the honour of Chriſts humane nature, and for his miniſterie in the world, the Saincts deceaſed alſo, <mn>◦</mn> being in heauen, haue gouernement ouer men and Prouinces, and therfore haue to doe with our affaires in the vvorld. Vvhich is againſt the Heretikes of theſe daies, that to take away our praiers to Saincts, vvould ſpoile them of many ſoueraine dignities, vvherein the Scriptures make them equal vvith Angels.

notes.text: Saincts also are Patrones, not only Angels.
